blocks.text: *Gear that shapes your kit, your defense, and your look.*
Weapons decide your skills

Your weapon is more than a stat stick — it **grants the active skills** on your hotbar (see *Skills*). Every weapon is a real 3D object your character holds, and swapping weapons swaps your whole kit.
The weapon roster

Every weapon owns a **distinct playstyle** — one clear reason to wield it. That playstyle isn't a design label: each of the twelve is the last surviving trace of one of the **Twelve Unwritten**, and how the weapon fights *is* how that person fought. None of them was ever named — only described by the deed witnesses remembered. They fall into three families:
Might — physical power, up close

rows: Win duels with precise single-target bursts and timed defense.
The One Who Cleared the Road
Delete whole groups with huge cleaves.
Deny enemies their turn — stun and knock them back.
The One Who Moved the Line
Reposition the fight — pull enemies in and impale them.
Protect your allies by absorbing all the attention. *(off-hand — pair it with a one-handed weapon)*

blocks.text: Finesse — precision & mobility

rows: Win through mobility and spacing — kite and never get touched.
Land one devastating shot, then reload.

blocks.text: Arcane — magic

rows: The One Who Burned the Field
Dominate whole areas with destructive magic.
The One Who Brought Them Back
Slowly overwhelm enemies with stacking curses.

blocks.text: Each weapon type has a deep pool of skills, and **every weapon that drops rolls its own kit** from that pool — which skills surface is pure chance, so no two of the same weapon play exactly alike. You can then shape it further at the forge. See *Skills* for how kits roll, and *Crafting & Recycling* for reforging, refining, transmog, and turning unwanted weapons into Essence.
Equipment slots
Beyond your weapon, you wear:

items: Your **Ring** — the vessel of your growth (see *Stats & the Ring*)

blocks.text: Each piece adds stats and defense; some carry set flavor or elemental properties.
Refinement (+N)
Gear can be **refined** to higher plus-levels:

items: A **weapon** gains **+3 Attack per refine level**.
**Every** piece of gear gains **+1 Defense per refine level**.

blocks.text: So a +10 weapon is +30 Attack over its base, and any +10 piece is +10 Defense.
Quality

Every piece you make carries a **quality grade**. A freshly forged piece is **Raw**; above that the ladder runs **F, E, D, C, B, A**, and A is the best there is. Quality is decided by the **quench** — the one moment of luck in a whole piece's making — and it moves one rung at a time, up or down, never in a jump.

**Quality decides four things.** How far a piece can be **folded**, which is what its attack or defence is made of; how much that fold total is **lifted**; how many **stats** can be written onto it with Ink; and how far your **mastery** with it can go. A fine blade does not swing harder by itself — it lets you become better with it than a poor one ever will.
Where a weapon's skills come from

**A weapon carries no skills.** You learn them yourself, by fighting with that kind of weapon: every skill names the **mastery level** at which it opens, and some name a skill you must know first. What you have learned is yours for good — the weapon in your hands only decides which of them you may use, and how much further you can still learn.
So two people holding the same sword do not have the same skills: they have the skills they each practised for.

So **seven skills is typical**, and about **one weapon in sixteen** drops with the full nine. Only the **Sword**'s skill pool is finished today — every other weapon type currently drops with no skills at all until its pool is written.
Cards
Some gear has **card slots** you can socket with cards for monster-matchup bonuses. See **Cards**.
